sanskrit: ambovāca apanītāsmi bhīṣmeṇa bhagavann avijānatā na hi jānāti me bhīṣmo brahmañ śālvagataṃ manaḥ
english: Ambā said: I was carried off by Bhīṣma, holy one, who did not know my heart; for Bhīṣma does not know, O brāhmaṇa, that my mind was set upon Śālva.

sanskrit: etad vicārya manasā bhavān eva viniścayam vicinotu yathānyāyaṃ vidhānaṃ kriyatāṃ tathā
english: Weighing this in your mind, let your honour himself reach the decision rightly, and let the remedy be made accordingly.

sanskrit: bhīṣme vā kuruśārdūle śālvarāje 'tha vā punaḥ ubhayor eva vā brahman yad yuktaṃ tat samācara
english: Whether against Bhīṣma, that tiger of the Kurus, or else against King Śālva, or indeed against them both, O brāhmaṇa—do what is fitting.

sanskrit: niveditaṃ mayā hy etad duḥkhamūlaṃ yathātatham vidhānaṃ tatra bhagavan kartum arhasi yuktitaḥ
english: For I have laid before you the root of my sorrow just as it is; in this matter, holy one, you ought to provide a remedy by sound reason.

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca upapannam idaṃ bhadre yad evaṃ varavarṇini dharmaṃ prati vaco brūyāḥ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: This is fitting, gentle and lovely lady, that you should speak thus in regard to what is right; now hear these words of mine.

sanskrit: yadi tvām āpageyo vai na nayed gajasāhvayam śālvas tvāṃ śirasā bhīru gṛhṇīyād rāmacoditaḥ
english: If the son of the River had not borne you off to the City named for the Elephant, then Śālva, O timid one, urged on by Rāma, would have received you with bowed head.

sanskrit: tena tvaṃ nirjitā bhadre yasmān nītāsi bhāmini saṃśayaḥ śālvarājasya tena tvayi sumadhyame
english: Because you were won by him, gentle lady, because you were carried off, O passionate one, therefore is King Śālva in doubt concerning you, slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ puruṣamānī ca jitakāśī tathaiva ca tasmāt pratikriyā yuktā bhīṣme kārayituṃ tvayā
english: Bhīṣma too is proud of his manhood and exults in his victories; therefore it is fitting that you have redress exacted from Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: ambovāca mamāpy eṣa mahān brahman hṛdi kāmo 'bhivartate ghātayeyaṃ yadi raṇe bhīṣmam ity eva nityadā
english: Ambā said: In my heart too, O brāhmaṇa, this great longing ever stirs—that I might have Bhīṣma slain in battle, this and nothing else, always.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ vā śālvarājaṃ vā yaṃ vā doṣeṇa gacchasi praśādhi taṃ mahābāho yatkṛte 'haṃ suduḥkhitā
english: Whether Bhīṣma or King Śālva—whomever you find at fault—chastise that one, O mighty-armed one, on whose account I am so deeply afflicted.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ kathayatām eva teṣāṃ sa divaso gataḥ rātriś ca bharataśreṣṭha sukhaśītoṣṇamārutā
english: Bhīṣma said: As they were thus conversing, that day passed away, and the night too, O best of the Bhāratas, with its breezes pleasantly cool and warm.

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ prādurāsīt prajvalann iva tejasā śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto rājañ jaṭācīradharo muniḥ
english: Then Rāma appeared, blazing as it were with his splendour, surrounded by his disciples, O king—the sage wearing matted locks and garments of bark.

sanskrit: dhanuṣpāṇir adīnātmā khaḍgaṃ bibhrat paraśvadhī virajā rājaśārdūla so 'bhyayāt sṛñjayaṃ nṛpam
english: Bow in hand, undaunted in spirit, bearing a sword and an axe, stainless, O tiger among kings, he approached the Sṛñjaya king.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ tāpasā dṛṣṭvā sa ca rājā mahātapāḥ tasthuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve sā ca kanyā tapasvinī
english: Then the ascetics, seeing him, and that king of great austerity, all stood with palms joined together—and so too that suffering maiden.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsur avyagrā madhuparkeṇa bhārgavam arcitaś ca yathāyogaṃ niṣasāda sahaiva taiḥ
english: Calmly they honoured the descendant of Bhṛgu with the honey-offering; and, duly worshipped, he sat down together with them.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrvavyatītāni kathayete sma tāv ubhau sṛñjayaś ca sa rājarṣir jāmadagnyaś ca bhārata
english: Then the two of them recounted to each other the things of bygone days—both that royal sage of the Sṛñjayas and the son of Jamadagni, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathānte rājarṣir bhṛguśreṣṭhaṃ mahābalam uvāca madhuraṃ kāle rāmaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: Then, when the talk was done, the royal sage at the right moment spoke to Rāma, that mighty best of the Bhṛgus, in sweet and meaningful words.

sanskrit: rāmeyaṃ mama dauhitrī kāśirājasutā prabho asyāḥ śṛṇu yathātattvaṃ kāryaṃ kāryaviśārada
english: Rāma, this is my daughter's daughter, the child of the king of Kāśi, O lord; hear her cause just as it truly stands, O you skilled in counsel.

sanskrit: paramaṃ kathyatāṃ ceti tāṃ rāmaḥ pratyabhāṣata tataḥ sābhyagamad rāmaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam
english: "Let her tell it fully," Rāma answered him; and then she approached Rāma, who blazed like fire itself.

sanskrit: sā cābhivādya caraṇau rāmasya śirasā śubhā spṛṣṭvā padmadalābhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyām agrataḥ sthitā
english: And that fair maiden, saluting Rāma's feet with her head and touching them with hands like lotus petals, stood before him.

sanskrit: ruroda sā śokavatī bāṣpavyākulalocanā prapede śaraṇaṃ caiva śaraṇyaṃ bhṛgunandanam
english: Stricken with grief, her eyes troubled with tears, she wept, and sought refuge with the son of Bhṛgu, the giver of refuge.

sanskrit: rāma uvāca yathāsi sṛñjayasyāsya tathā mama nṛpātmaje brūhi yat te manoduḥkhaṃ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava
english: Rāma said: As you are to this Sṛñjaya king, so are you to me, O daughter of a king. Tell me the sorrow of your heart; I shall do your bidding.

sanskrit: ambovāca bhagavañ śaraṇaṃ tvādya prapannāsmi mahāvrata śokapaṅkārṇavād ghorād uddharasva ca māṃ vibho
english: Ambā said: Holy one of mighty vows, this day I have come to you for refuge; lift me out of the dreadful ocean whose mire is sorrow, O lord.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tasyāś ca dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ca vayaś cābhinavaṃ punaḥ saukumāryaṃ paraṃ caiva rāmaś cintāparo 'bhavat
english: Bhīṣma said: Beholding her beauty, her tender youth, and her exceeding delicacy, Rāma fell to brooding thought.

sanskrit: kim iyaṃ vakṣyatīty evaṃ vimṛśan bhṛgusattamaḥ iti dadhyau ciraṃ rāmaḥ kṛpayābhipariplutaḥ
english: "What will she say?" Thus the best of the Bhṛgus pondered; long did Rāma meditate, overwhelmed with compassion.

sanskrit: kathyatām iti sā bhūyo rāmeṇoktā śucismitā sarvam eva yathātattvaṃ kathayām āsa bhārgave
english: "Tell it," Rāma said to her again; and she of the bright smile recounted everything just as it truly was to the descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā jāmadagnyas tu rājaputryā vacas tadā uvāca tāṃ varārohāṃ niścityārthaviniścayam
english: Hearing then the words of the king's daughter, the son of Jamadagni, having settled the certain conclusion of the matter, said to her of the fair hips:

sanskrit: preṣayiṣyāmi bhīṣmāya kuruśreṣṭhāya bhāmini kariṣyati vaco dharmyaṃ śrutvā me sa narādhipaḥ
english: I shall send word to Bhīṣma, best of the Kurus, O passionate lady; that ruler of men, on hearing me, will carry out my righteous command.

sanskrit: na cet kariṣyati vaco mayoktaṃ jāhnavīsutaḥ dhakṣyāmy enaṃ raṇe bhadre sāmātyaṃ śastratejasā
english: But if the son of Jāhnavī will not do as I bid, then in battle, gentle lady, I shall burn him up, ministers and all, with the fire of my weapons.

sanskrit: atha vā te matis tatra rājaputri nivartate tāvac chālvapatiṃ vīraṃ yojayāmy atra karmaṇi
english: Or else, O king's daughter, if your mind turns away from that, then I shall instead set the heroic lord of Śālva to this task.

sanskrit: ambovāca visarjitāsmi bhīṣmeṇa śrutvaiva bhṛgunandana śālvarājagataṃ ceto mama pūrvaṃ manīṣitam
english: Ambā said: I was let go by Bhīṣma, O son of Bhṛgu, as soon as he heard that my heart had long before been resolved upon King Śālva.

sanskrit: saubharājam upetyāham abruvaṃ durvacaṃ vacaḥ na ca māṃ pratyagṛhṇāt sa cāritrapariśaṅkitaḥ
english: Going to the lord of Saubha, I spoke words hard to utter; but he would not receive me back, mistrustful of my conduct.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ viniścitya svabuddhyā bhṛgunandana yad atraupayikaṃ kāryaṃ tac cintayitum arhasi
english: Weighing all this with your own judgement, O son of Bhṛgu, you ought to consider what course of action is here the fitting one.

sanskrit: mamātra vyasanasyāsya bhīṣmo mūlaṃ mahāvrataḥ yenāhaṃ vaśam ānītā samutkṣipya balāt tadā
english: The root of this calamity of mine is Bhīṣma of the mighty vow, by whom I was then seized up by force and brought under his power.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ jahi mahābāho yatkṛte duḥkham īdṛśam prāptāhaṃ bhṛguśārdūla carāmy apriyam uttamam
english: Slay Bhīṣma, O mighty-armed one, on whose account such sorrow has befallen me; for his sake, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, I wander on in utmost misery.

sanskrit: sa hi lubdhaś ca mānī ca jitakāśī ca bhārgava tasmāt pratikriyā kartuṃ yuktā tasmai tvayānagha
english: For he is greedy, and proud, and exultant in victory, O descendant of Bhṛgu; therefore it is fitting that you exact redress upon him, O sinless one.

sanskrit: eṣa me hriyamāṇāyā bhāratena tadā vibho abhavad dhṛdi saṃkalpo ghātayeyaṃ mahāvratam
english: This was the resolve that arose in my heart, O lord, when I was being carried off by the Bhārata: that I would have him of the mighty vow slain.

sanskrit: tasmāt kāmaṃ mamādyemaṃ rāma saṃvartayānagha jahi bhīṣmaṃ mahābāho yathā vṛtraṃ puraṃdaraḥ
english: Therefore fulfil this longing of mine this day, O sinless Rāma; slay Bhīṣma, mighty-armed one, as Purandara slew Vṛtra.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktas tadā rāmo jahi bhīṣmam iti prabho uvāca rudatīṃ kanyāṃ codayantīṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed with "Slay Bhīṣma," O lord, Rāma then spoke to the weeping maiden, who urged him again and again:

sanskrit: kāśye kāmaṃ na gṛhṇāmi śastraṃ vai varavarṇini ṛte brahmavidāṃ hetoḥ kim anyat karavāṇi te
english: O daughter of Kāśi, willingly I take up no weapon, lovely lady, save for the sake of the knowers of the Veda. What else can I do for you?

sanskrit: vācā bhīṣmaś ca śālvaś ca mama rājñi vaśānugau bhaviṣyato 'navadyāṅgi tat kariṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
english: By my word both Bhīṣma and Śālva, O queenly one, shall become obedient to my will, O flawless-limbed one; that I shall do—grieve not.

sanskrit: na tu śastraṃ grahīṣyāmi kathaṃ cid api bhāmini ṛte niyogād viprāṇām eṣa me samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: But by no means whatever shall I take up a weapon, O passionate lady, except at the bidding of the brāhmaṇas; this is the vow I have made.

sanskrit: ambovāca mama duḥkhaṃ bhagavatā vyapaneyaṃ yatas tataḥ tat tu bhīṣmaprasūtaṃ me taṃ jahīśvara māciram
english: Ambā said: My sorrow must by all means be taken away by your honour; and since it is Bhīṣma who has begotten it for me, slay him, O lord, without delay.

sanskrit: rāma uvāca kāśikanye punar brūhi bhīṣmas te caraṇāv ubhau śirasā vandanārho 'pi grahīṣyati girā mama
english: Rāma said: Speak once more, maiden of Kāśi: Bhīṣma, though himself worthy to be revered, will at my word take hold of both your feet with his head.

sanskrit: ambovāca jahi bhīṣmaṃ raṇe rāma mama ced icchasi priyam pratiśrutaṃ ca yadi tat satyaṃ kartum ihārhasi
english: Ambā said: Slay Bhīṣma in battle, Rāma, if you wish to do me a kindness; and if that was promised, you ought here to make it come true.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tayoḥ saṃvadator evaṃ rājan rāmāmbayos tadā akṛtavraṇo jāmadagnyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Bhīṣma said: As the two of them, Rāma and Ambā, were thus conversing, O king, Akṛtavraṇa spoke these words to the son of Jamadagni:

sanskrit: śaraṇāgatāṃ mahābāho kanyāṃ na tyaktum arhasi jahi bhīṣmaṃ raṇe rāma garjantam asuraṃ yathā
english: O mighty-armed one, you ought not to abandon a maiden who has come to you for refuge; slay Bhīṣma in battle, Rāma, as one slays a roaring demon.

sanskrit: yadi bhīṣmas tvayāhūto raṇe rāma mahāmune nirjito 'smīti vā brūyāt kuryād vā vacanaṃ tava
english: If Bhīṣma, summoned by you to battle, Rāma, O great sage, should say "I am vanquished," or should do your bidding,

sanskrit: kṛtam asyā bhavet kāryaṃ kanyāyā bhṛgunandana vākyaṃ satyaṃ ca te vīra bhaviṣyati kṛtaṃ vibho
english: then this maiden's cause would be accomplished, O son of Bhṛgu, and your word, O hero, would be made true and fulfilled, O lord.

sanskrit: iyaṃ cāpi pratijñā te tadā rāma mahāmune jitvā vai kṣatriyān sarvān brāhmaṇeṣu pratiśrutam
english: And this too was the vow you once made, Rāma, O great sage, when, having conquered all the kṣatriyas, you gave your pledge before the brāhmaṇas:

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdraś caiva raṇe yadi brahmadviḍ bhavitā taṃ vai haniṣyāmīti bhārgava
english: "If in battle a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, or even a śūdra shall prove a hater of the brāhmaṇas, him will I slay"—so you swore, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ hi prapannānāṃ bhītānāṃ jīvitārthinām na śakṣyāmi parityāgaṃ kartuṃ jīvan kathaṃ cana
english: "Of those who come to me for refuge, frightened and longing to live, I shall never be able, so long as I live, to forsake any."

sanskrit: yaś ca kṣatraṃ raṇe kṛtsnaṃ vijeṣyati samāgatam dṛptātmānam ahaṃ taṃ ca haniṣyāmīti bhārgava
english: "And whoever shall vanquish in battle the whole kṣatriya host assembled, him too, that arrogant one, will I slay"—so you swore, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ vijayī rāma bhīṣmaḥ kurukulodvahaḥ tena yudhyasva saṃgrāme sametya bhṛgunandana
english: Now Bhīṣma, the upholder of the Kuru line, is just such a conqueror, Rāma; meet him and fight with him in combat, O son of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: rāma uvāca smarāmy ahaṃ pūrvakṛtāṃ pratijñām ṛṣisattama tathaiva ca kariṣyāmi yathā sāmnaiva lapsyate
english: Rāma said: I remember the vow I made of old, O best of sages, and I shall act accordingly—yet so that the end may first be gained by conciliation.

sanskrit: kāryam etan mahad brahman kāśikanyāmanogatam gamiṣyāmi svayaṃ tatra kanyām ādāya yatra saḥ
english: This is a great matter, O brāhmaṇa, that dwells in the heart of the maiden of Kāśi; I shall go there myself, taking the maiden, to where he is.

sanskrit: yadi bhīṣmo raṇaślāghī na kariṣyati me vacaḥ haniṣyāmy enam udriktam iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: If Bhīṣma, who glories in battle, will not do as I say, then I shall slay that overweening one; such is my settled resolve.

sanskrit: na hi bāṇā mayotsṛṣṭāḥ sajjantīha śarīriṇām kāyeṣu viditaṃ tubhyaṃ purā kṣatriyasaṃgare
english: For the arrows loosed by me do not cling fast in the bodies of living beings—as is known to you from of old, in my battles with the kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā tato rāmaḥ saha tair brahmavādibhiḥ prayāṇāya matiṃ kṛtvā samuttasthau mahāmanāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, Rāma then, together with those expounders of the Veda, resolved upon setting forth, and the great-souled one rose up.

sanskrit: tatas te tām uṣitvā tu rajanīṃ tatra tāpasāḥ hutāgnayo japtajapyāḥ pratasthur majjighāṃsayā
english: Then those ascetics, having passed that night there, having offered into the fire and murmured their prayers, set out with the desire to have me slain.

sanskrit: abhyagacchat tato rāmaḥ saha tair brāhmaṇarṣabhaiḥ kurukṣetraṃ mahārāja kanyayā saha bhārata
english: Then Rāma, together with those bulls among brāhmaṇas, came to Kurukṣetra, O great king, along with the maiden, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nyaviśanta tataḥ sarve parigṛhya sarasvatīm tāpasās te mahātmāno bhṛguśreṣṭhapuraskṛtāḥ
english: Then they all encamped, having taken up their station along the Sarasvatī—those great-souled ascetics, with the best of the Bhṛgus at their head.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tṛtīye divase same deśe vyavasthitaḥ preṣayām āsa me rājan prāpto 'smīti mahāvrataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, on the third day, taking his stand upon level ground, he of the mighty vow sent word to me, O king: "I have arrived."

sanskrit: tam āgatam ahaṃ śrutvā viṣayāntaṃ mahābalam abhyagacchaṃ javenāśu prītyā tejonidhiṃ prabhum
english: Hearing that the mighty one had come to the border of the realm, I went swiftly forth to meet him with joy—that lord who was a treasury of splendour.

sanskrit: gāṃ puraskṛtya rājendra brāhmaṇaiḥ parivāritaḥ ṛtvigbhir devakalpaiś ca tathaiva ca purohitaiḥ
english: Putting a cow before me, O king of kings, surrounded by brāhmaṇas, by priests of the sacrifice godlike in their nature, and likewise by household chaplains.

sanskrit: sa mām abhigataṃ dṛṣṭvā jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān pratijagrāha tāṃ pūjāṃ vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Seeing me come to him, the valiant son of Jamadagni accepted that worship and spoke these words:

sanskrit: bhīṣma kāṃ buddhim āsthāya kāśirājasutā tvayā akāmeyam ihānītā punaś caiva visarjitā
english: Bhīṣma, with what intent was this daughter of the king of Kāśi brought here by you against her will, and then again sent away?

sanskrit: vibhraṃśitā tvayā hīyaṃ dharmāvāpteḥ parāvarāt parāmṛṣṭāṃ tvayā hīmāṃ ko hi gantum ihārhati
english: For by you she has been made to fall from the winning of righteousness, in its higher and lower forms; and who indeed could now take her, whom you have laid hands upon?

sanskrit: pratyākhyātā hi śālvena tvayā nīteti bhārata tasmād imāṃ manniyogāt pratigṛhṇīṣva bhārata
english: For she has been rejected by Śālva, saying "she was carried off by you," O Bhārata; therefore, at my command, take her back, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: svadharmaṃ puruṣavyāghra rājaputrī labhatv iyam na yuktam avamāno 'yaṃ kartuṃ rājñā tvayānagha
english: Let this king's daughter, O tiger among men, attain her own proper estate; it is not fitting that this slight should be put upon her by you, a king, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ nātimanasaṃ samudīkṣyāham abruvam nāham enāṃ punar dadyāṃ bhrātre brahman kathaṃ cana
english: Then, looking upon him whose mind was ill at ease, I said: I shall in no way give her again to my brother, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: śālvasyāham iti prāha purā mām iha bhārgava mayā caivābhyanujñātā gatā saubhapuraṃ prati
english: "I belong to Śālva," she declared to me here long ago, O descendant of Bhṛgu; and granted leave by me, she went off toward the city of Saubha.

sanskrit: na bhayān nāpy anukrośān na lobhān nārthakāmyayā kṣatradharmam ahaṃ jahyām iti me vratam āhitam
english: Neither out of fear, nor out of pity, nor out of greed, nor from desire of gain shall I abandon the kṣatriya's law; such is the vow I have laid upon myself.

sanskrit: atha mām abravīd rāmaḥ krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ na kariṣyasi ced etad vākyaṃ me kurupuṃgava
english: Then Rāma, his eyes troubled with wrath, said to me: If you will not do as these words of mine require, O bull of the Kurus,

sanskrit: haniṣyāmi sahāmātyaṃ tvām adyeti punaḥ punaḥ saṃrambhād abravīd rāmaḥ krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
english: "I shall slay you this very day, ministers and all"—so again and again, in his fury, Rāma spoke, his eyes troubled with wrath.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ gīrbhir iṣṭābhiḥ punaḥ punar ariṃdamam ayācaṃ bhṛguśārdūlaṃ na caiva praśaśāma saḥ
english: With pleasing words I again and again entreated that subduer of foes, that tiger of the Bhṛgus; yet he would not be appeased.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ praṇamya śirasā bhūyo brāhmaṇasattamam abruvaṃ kāraṇaṃ kiṃ tad yat tvaṃ yoddhum ihecchasi
english: Bowing my head once more to that best of brāhmaṇas, I said: What is the reason for which you wish to fight with me here?

sanskrit: iṣvastraṃ mama bālasya bhavataiva caturvidham upadiṣṭaṃ mahābāho śiṣyo 'smi tava bhārgava
english: The fourfold science of missile and weapon was taught to me, when I was a boy, by you yourself, O mighty-armed one; I am your pupil, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd rāmaḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ jānīṣe māṃ guruṃ bhīṣma na cemāṃ pratigṛhṇase sutāṃ kāśyasya kauravya matpriyārthaṃ mahīpate
english: Then Rāma, his eyes red with anger, said to me: You know me to be your teacher, Bhīṣma, and yet you will not take back this daughter of the king of Kāśi to please me, O Kaurava, O lord of the earth?

sanskrit: na hi te vidyate śāntir anyathā kurunandana gṛhāṇemāṃ mahābāho rakṣasva kulam ātmanaḥ tvayā vibhraṃśitā hīyaṃ bhartāraṃ nābhigacchati
english: For in no other way is there peace for you, O joy of the Kurus; take her, mighty-armed one, and preserve your own line. For she, made to fall by you, can win no husband.
